plan.title: bug(design-critique): ingest-ready must not stamp when Stop 1 warrant pain is unrelieved

narratives.Description: Ingest-ready must not stamp when named Stop 1 warrant pains are unrelieved. Coverage lives on evaluateCompletedArcRecord so a valid-looking synthesis still returns blocked and ingest rejects the leftover Bound-remedy window.
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR:** `design-critique:ingest-ready` is not valid when the accepted lean does not relieve the Stop 1 warrant pain. All-accept of critic headings is not pain coverage. The parent must escalate the unrelieved conjuncts and either run another round or stop for a human. Do not ingest.

## Problem

Stop 1 records why the arc was warranted:

```text
design-critique: warranted, because …
```

`verify:judgment-gates` checks presence, shape, and authority. It never scores the because-clause (ADR-005). Auto-stamp then binds on critic-heading totality: every classified heading `accept-into-contract`, operator confirm (yolo counts), no leftover critic residual. `resolveAutoStampCatalogChip` writes `design-critique:ingest-ready`.

That denominator never asks whether Bound-remedy covers the warrant. A recut can *admit the pain is leftover*, harvest two forbids plus an unrelated bug fix, and still auto-stamp ingest-ready.

#4205 tried a `recut-needed` chip so Recut leans would not leave the bind chip. #4298 retired that chip. `Spec-path:` / `Recut:` is a lean token. Auto-stamp still writes ingest-ready. The hole is back, and it is larger than recut: any all-accept lean can drop the warrant pain.

Chip is list state, not consent. Ingest keys off the completed-arc record. So this is not only a label miss. The completed-arc record itself must not clear ingest while warrant pain is unrelieved.

## Exemplar: #4378

Stop 1 warrant (comment 5654639130):

> USER.md onboarding is still a 13-question chat loop with no detect-then-confirm, no import from other agents, and no real provenance.

Successor lean 5654755223 Bound-remedy:

1. Personal always-wins stays operator-authored. Imported repo files do not write USER.md Personal.
2. Reuse existing step protocol. Do not add a parallel wizard RPC.
3. Version-stamp bug: use the live version source, not a generated reader worse than the bug.

The lean's own plain English still says USER.md onboarding lacks detect-then-confirm and import. Synthesis accepted because agents agreed (empty disagreement set). Chip is `design-critique:ingest-ready`.

| Pain (warrant conjunct) | Relieved? | Why the lean does not |
|---|---|---|
| Detect-then-confirm in Phase 1 | no | Bound-remedy has no detect path. Critics correctly blocked writing Phase 2 fields into USER.md; that refusal is not a replacement. |
| Import from other agents | no | Bound-remedy 1 forbids repo-file to Personal. That prevents new harm. It does not bind a safe import. |
| Real provenance | no | Bound-remedy 3 stamps installed version. A version string is not last-run / source / destination provenance. |
| Blank chat loop | no | Bound-remedy 2 keeps the existing interview protocol. |

The stamp fix is a real defect and may ship as its own slice. It is not one of the three warrant conjuncts. Spec-path harvest of forbids-plus-unrelated-bug-fix is not relief.

N=3 panel on #4378 is spent (no default retry). Silent round 2 on the same envelope is dual-stop illegal. The skill must escalate to a later arc, an operator-amended lean that actually binds relief, or halt if the operator accepts stamp-only as a warrant change.

## Proposal

Coverage of the recorded warrant is a bind conjunct. Do not NLP-grade whether the warrant was *true*. Check whether named pains are covered.

1. **Stop 1 records `pain:` as a list.** The because-clause stays for humans. The list is what bind reads. One conjunct per item. Derived from the because-clause at write-back time.
2. **Successor-lean Bound-remedy items cite pain ids they relieve, or `does-not-relieve`.** Uncited pain stays residual. Map is not total.
3. **Parent posts a pain-coverage table before any bind path.** Columns: pain, relieved?, why not. Token a closed line such as `design-critique: pain-unrelieved, because …` when any row is unrelieved and not `operator-deferred`.
4. **Unrelieved pain blocks auto-stamp and bind path 2.** Do not write `design-critique:ingest-ready`. Do not post `design-critique: synthesis accepted, because agents agreed (empty disagreement set)` as ingest clearance. Print **retry differences**, or if dual-stop is spent, halt for human / later-arc. Do not print ingest.
5. **`operator-deferred` is explicit.** A named later slice, recorded on the lean, is the only way to leave a warrant conjunct unbound and still stamp. Silent Spec-path leftover is not defer.
6. **Keep ADR-005.** Engine still does not judge warrant quality, truth, or sufficiency. It refuses to stamp when named pains are uncovered.

Thin skill (`deft-directive-design-critique`) stays a pointer. Normative rules live in `content/contracts/design-critique.md`. Content-contract tests lock the new refusal. Auto-stamp resolver grows a coverage conjunct, not a prose parser.

## Non-goals

- Scoring whether the Stop 1 because-clause was a good reason to run an arc.
- Restoring `design-critique:recut-needed` as a catalog chip (#4298 closed that catalog).
- NLP classification of lean English (`Spec-path:` stays a line-start token).
- Implementing the #4378 product recut (safe import, Phase-1 detect that is not project-stack-into-Personal, provenance that is not a version digit). That is a later arc on #4378 after this bind rule exists. Shipping that arc first will re-fire the same auto-stamp.

## Acceptance sketch

- Given a Stop 1 `pain:` list and a Bound-remedy that does not cite those ids as relieved or operator-deferred, auto-stamp does not write ingest-ready and does not emit the empty-disagreement synthesis-accepted line as ingest clearance.
- Parent posts the coverage table naming each unrelieved conjunct and why the current lean does not relieve it.
- Dual-stop spent plus unrelieved pain prints halt-for-human or later-arc, not ingest.
- A lean that relieves every pain id (or records operator-deferred with a named later slice) may still auto-stamp as today.
- ADR-005 tests still never score because-clause content.
- #4378 is the fixture: warrant conjuncts vs lean 5654755223 Bound-remedy must fail coverage.

Relates #4378 (exemplar), #4205 (recut-needed chip), #4298 (chip retired; Recut: token still stamps ingest-ready), #3640 (all-accept auto-stamp), #3806 (ingest waits on completed-arc record), ADR-005 (because-clause never scored for quality).

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-13T21:45:24Z)

model: gpt-6
role: critic

Round 1, fresh refutation. Input ceiling: 5656317654. Source SHA: b9511febc28cd6d08e3280a0c5cd05f05e38b4bc. Process-only; no sibling posts read.

The premise survives: accepting every critic heading does not establish coverage of the recorded warrant. The proposed remedy cannot bind as written because its admission and authority boundaries remain underspecified.

Re-verification: REST reads of #4378 comments 5654639130 and 5654755223 confirm the quoted warrant and the three Bound-remedy items. This confirms the documentary mismatch, not the truth of the original onboarding claims. I transpiled SHA-pinned completed-arc-record.ts, citation-grammar.ts, exclusive-chip.ts, and auto-stamp-chip.ts into OS temporary storage and executed a synthetic thread: Stop 1 names P1; the lean explicitly says its version fix does not relieve P1; a synthesis cites that lean. evaluateCompletedArcRecord returned status=complete, and resolveAutoStampCatalogChip returned design-critique:ingest-ready. This is a current-code counterexample, not a test of an implemented proposal.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Put the refusal at ingest admission, not only the chip resolver

Evidence: packages/core/src/design-critique/auto-stamp-chip.ts ignores its optional lean-body argument and returns the catalog constant. completed-arc-record.ts independently admits the latest cited lean; its closed refusal set has no pain-coverage state. The executable counterexample above passes without consulting a coverage table. The proposal recognizes the completed-record problem, but its implementation paragraph and acceptance sketch concentrate on the resolver and parent posting behavior.

Failure: a manual, old, or mistaken synthesis record still clears ingest even if the new resolver refuses its label. Catalog state is expressly not clearance.

Consequence: require the existing completed-arc admission path to consume the same bounded coverage verdict used before either bind path. Publish the refusal reason and one remediation. Test a valid-looking synthesis with missing/unrelieved coverage, including explicit operator-accept synthesis, and prove ingest refuses regardless of labels. Content-contract string tests alone do not establish this behavior. Reuse this admission point rather than adding another independent gate.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Specify which warrant and coverage record bind

Evidence: proposal items 1–3 introduce pain ids, remedy references, and a table, but no closed grammar or revision-selection rule. The contract allows multiple arcs on one issue. The cited #4378 Stop 1 has no pain list at all. Existing latest-lean selection and citation parsing solve related artifact-selection problems, but do not select a pain denominator.

Failure: an empty or absent list can pass vacuously; a later smaller list or an old coverage table can erase unresolved pain. Applying the new rule to the raw #4378 fixture also requires a legacy policy: no parser can recover its proposed ids without interpreting prose.

Consequence: define a non-vacuous, revision-bound denominator and a coverage record tied to the accepted lean and originating warrant. State missing/malformed/duplicate/unknown-id behavior and how a superseding warrant is authorized. Choose and document legacy handling; use an explicitly annotated #4378 fixture if migration is not intended. Reuse the citation grammar and position handling. Under the injection/shared-thread lens, quoted examples and unrelated comments must not create, replace, or discharge the denominator. This does not require NLP grading.

### 3. blocks-the-design — A relief reference is an assertion; a named later slice is not operator consent

Evidence: proposal items 2 and 5 permit relief citations or operator-deferred with a named later slice. The existing Parent-side substantiation rules already require independent audit of a new load-bearing parent premise while adjudicating findings, and forbid parent self-clearance. Yolo confirms an all-accept critic map; it does not currently authorize a newly introduced pain-deferral operation.

Failure: the parent can annotate the same unrelated version fix as relieving all pain ids, or name a future slice and call every row operator-deferred. Membership passes while the original pain remains. A coverage table by the same author adds no independent evidence.

Consequence: describe the deterministic claim narrowly as recorded disposition coverage. Retain ADR-006 for newly introduced relief premises; identify evidence or already audited critic findings supporting each relief claim. Require an explicit operator decision tied to the particular pain ids and destination slice for deferral, and state whether standing yolo can authorize that scope change. A future slice name alone cannot serve as the operator decision. No new identity system or semantic scorer is needed.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Distinguish accepting a bounded remedy from solving the whole warrant

Evidence: proposal item 5 permits explicit deferral, while the headline premise says unrelieved pain must never stamp. The contract also permits an operator to raise the N=3 post cap and record it; a fourth post is not categorically forbidden. Pre-bind lean revisions stay inside the current arc.

Failure: absolute relief language obscures the allowed bounded-slice outcome and can send an operator into an unnecessary later arc or imply that ingest readiness means implementation has already relieved the pain.

Consequence: say that every named pain needs a supported bound remedy or an authorized explicit deferral before admission. Keep unresolved coverage residual; offer a recorded cap increase or halt when the default budget is spent. A later arc is not required merely because the lean changes before bind.

Road not taken: a syntax-only table plus chip-resolver change is attractive because it is small and preserves ADR-005, but it leaves the demonstrated admission bypass and parent self-attestation hole. I would change that verdict with one shared coverage evaluator wired into existing admission, an explicit legacy/revision contract, and reuse of the existing audit and operator-decision rules.

The hole is real. Critic-heading all-accept is not warrant coverage. The proposed control does not bind as written.

## 1. Coverage must refuse ingest on evaluateCompletedArcRecord, not on the chip resolver

blocks-the-design

Evidence. At pin b9511febc28cd6d08e3280a0c5cd05f05e38b4bc, `resolveAutoStampCatalogChip` ignores its lean argument and always returns the ingest-ready catalog name (`packages/core/src/design-critique/auto-stamp-chip.ts`). The published block-reason set is missing-record, lone-shape, cite-not-lean, missing-table-cite, unshaped-table-cite, ambiguous-table-cite, cancelled, set-level-body, stale-target. No warrant-coverage row. The contract already forbids treating the ingest-ready chip as ingest clearance.

Re-verified #4378 fixture. Stop 1 comment 5654639130 names detect-then-confirm, import from other agents, and real provenance. Successor comment 5654755223 records residual none, all-accept, path-selector next-build not the body, and a Bound remedy of two forbids plus a version-stamp fix. Parent comment 5654759686 posts the path-1 empty-disagreement accepted line citing that lean. That record is ingest-complete independent of the chip.

Failure mode. A parent that still posts the path-1 accepted line (live parent turns are unenforced; auto-stamp is a recipe) still clears ingest while named pains are uncovered. Growing the chip resolver cannot close the hole the issue named: the completed-arc record itself must not clear.

Disposition. The lean cannot bind until coverage is a published completed-arc block reason, or an equivalent evaluator refusal of complete while named pains are uncovered. Content-contract string pins of parent-recipe text are not that gate.

## 2. operator-deferred plus yolo is leftover harvest with a token

blocks-the-design

Evidence. Proposal 4 says unrelieved pain blocks both bind paths and, when dual-stop is spent, halt or later-arc. Proposal 5 says operator-deferred is the only way to leave a warrant conjunct unbound and still stamp. #4378 spend was N>=3 (write-back 5654639130); dual-stop gives that panel no default retry. Yolo standing on a launching utterance is already the confirm conjunct for a posted all-accept map, including path-selector leans. `operatorVerbApplySet` prints no verbs when autoStamp is true.

Failure mode. The #4378 state (all-accept critic headings, Bound remedy that does not relieve the warrant, dual-stop spent) can be tokened operator-deferred with a named later slice on the same number, yolo-confirmed, harvested, and ingested. That is leftover path-selector harvest renamed. Same-number later slice is not a warrant change and is not halt.

Disposition. The lean cannot bind with operator-deferred as a stamp-enabler on the same issue. Same-number leftover is halt, or a later lean that actually binds relief, without ingest clearance. Deferred work, if it exists, needs a different issue id. That token is a load-bearing parent premise under parent-side substantiation, not yolo-confirmable leftover.

## 3. Pain-id cites detect omission; they do not prove relief

sharpens-framing

Evidence. Critic method: token presence is not behavioral evidence. ADR-005 / ADR-006 already refuse engine-graded because-clauses and parent self-clear of load-bearing premises. Uncited pain as residual in the existing auto-stamp denominator would make the map not total; retry and halt already exist. A separate pain-coverage comment is a third map type; the contract says the successor lean is the disposition map. A missing or one-item tautological pain list is the new silent omission. Relieved-row English is a parent premise after critics exist, so it is inside parent-side substantiation; the proposal never records those tokens.

Failure mode. After the cite grammar exists, a parent writes a one-item stamp-bug pain list, or cites detect/import/provenance on the three #4378 forbids. The engine reports covered. #4378 as a historical fixture fails only because those items have no cites yet.

Disposition. Bindable if: Stop 1 missing the pain list fails closed; uncited pain ids are residual headings on the successor lean (no third map); a relieved cite is an ADR-006 asserted premise a later critic must target; the engine still does not grade whether relief is true.

## 4. Coverage tokens are untrusted thread input

sharpens-framing

Evidence. This target changes ingest authority, envelopes, and shared completed-arc state, so the injection / swarm lens applies. Issue bodies, comments, and quoted Stop 1 fields are untrusted. Target-digest already uses classifyPosition; the path-1 accepted-sentence shape does not, and a fenced copy reclassifies. The proposal names pain lists, does-not-relieve, operator-deferred, and a closed pain-unrelieved line without an authority pin or position predicate.

Failure mode. A critic quote, fence, or later aside that carries those tokens changes coverage or mints a terminal record. Scanning the whole thread for pain items also lets a quote add conjuncts (fail-closed DoS) or, if last-writer wins, drop them.

Disposition. Parser authority is the Stop 1 write-back for the pain list and the cited successor lean for cites. Fence, quote, strike, and inline-code do not count. Publish any new block reason before the evaluator returns it. Do not restore recut-needed.

## 5. Exemplar chip is not currently ingest-ready

footnote

#4378 labels at this read are still mechanism-shaped. Later-arc parent comment 5655949239 (after #4496 was filed) supersedes lean 5654755223, so the older accepted record does not clear the latest lean. That recovery uses existing later-lean machinery. It does not put a coverage conjunct on ingest. The window to harvest the leftover Bound remedy was the completed record 5654759686, not the chip.

Injection / swarm. Identity, worktrees, and worker concurrency are not the blast. The blast is untrusted envelope fields deciding ingest. Closed tokens with position predicates are in. NLP of lean English and a restored recut-needed chip are out.

Road-not-taken. I looked at restoring recut-needed, at parent-recipe-only coverage, and at a human-only coverage confirm. Recut-needed is a chip, and chips are not clearance. Recipe-only coverage leaves a posted accepted line ingestible. A human confirm is waived by yolo standing. The mechanism that already fails closed on omission is denominator totality plus evaluateCompletedArcRecord.

Steelman of cite-ids-are-enough. Every working gate in this motion is a closed-token recording obligation. Named-pain cites are that family, and a false cite is an auditable lie in the same sense as a wrong mechanism-shaped stamp. What flips finding 2: operator-deferred must cite a different issue, cannot be yolo-confirmed, and is an unresolved audit marker until a critic targets it. What flips finding 1: the coverage conjunct lives in evaluateCompletedArcRecord with a published reason, and a posted empty-disagreement accepted line does not yield complete while that reason holds.

## Finding 1 — the named lever has no production caller

**blocks-the-design**

*Evidence.* `resolveAutoStampCatalogChip` (`packages/core/src/design-critique/auto-stamp-chip.ts:38`) at the pinned SHA:

```ts
export function resolveAutoStampCatalogChip(
  _successorLeanBody?: string,
): DesignCritiqueCatalogChip {
  return "design-critique:ingest-ready";
}
```

It ignores its only parameter and has no conditional. `git grep -l resolveAutoStampCatalogChip` over the whole pinned tree returns `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `content/commands.md`, `content/contracts/design-critique.md`, two test files, the module itself, and two completed xbriefs. **Zero production callers.** `evaluateParentAudit` (`parent-audit.ts:106`) is the same: zero non-test callers. The only live gate on the ingest path is `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest`, called once at `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:2027`.

The auto-stamp denominator the Problem section describes is not code. It is parent prose in `content/contracts/design-critique.md` under Operator verbs, executed by an agent.

*Failure mode.* Proposal 4 and the closing line "Auto-stamp resolver grows a coverage conjunct, not a prose parser" both land the guard on a fixture. The slice ships, content-contract tests go green, and the next parent that would have stamped a thin lean stamps it anyway — because the function carrying the new conjunct is never called on a live arc. This is the failure the contract has already recorded three times in this same layer: #3850 ("A parent that binds on a partial panel breaks this contract and no gate will stop it"), #3929, #4309.

*Disposition consequence.* Item 4 cannot bind as written. The lean must pick a surface and say which: parent prose (honest, unobserved, and then say so in the contract's own voice as the panel-completeness and summary sections do), or `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` (the one live gate — and then Findings 3 and 7 apply).

## Finding 2 — this is ADR-006 audit markers, minus non-self-clear

**blocks-the-design**

*Evidence.* The mechanism the Proposal describes already exists and is machine-evaluated. `evaluateParentAudit` computes unresolved load-bearing premises and fails closed on four codes: `parent-self-clear` (a `role: parent` artifact clearing its own marker), `silent-clear` (a marker dropped without critic clearance), `bind-unresolved` (`bind.allAcceptMap && unresolvedForBind.length > 0`), and `envelope-omits-target` (the next critic envelope failing to name the marker). `independentlyCleared` requires `clearedByRole === "critic" && targetsMarker`. The contract already carries the forbid on auto-stamping while any audit marker is unresolved, and the auto-bind conjunct already reads "all-accept disposition map AND zero unresolved audit markers AND …".

The only reason #4378 escaped that machinery is an express carve-out in `## Parent-side substantiation`: *"A load-bearing premise introduced before any critic exists is outside this obligation. At Stop 1 nobody has spoken and the entire critic pass is the audit."* The same section records that #3651's round-1 critic raised exactly this boundary and that the successor lean deliberately settled it. Stop 1 also already records `refutation-target:`, which on #4378 (`5654639130`) is verbatim the three pains — and the contract forbids treating that field as an `audit:` marker, because "the field creates no unresolved-marker state and never blocks bind."

So Proposal 1's `pain:` is `refutation-target:` with teeth, and this issue never names the decision it is reversing.

*Failure mode.* The parallel drops non-self-clear. Proposal 3 has the **parent** post the coverage table and the **parent** fill the `relieved?` column. On #4378 the same `grok-4.6` authored Stop 1, the thin lean `5654755223`, and the recut `5655949239` — whose own pain-coverage table marks all six rows `yes`. A parent willing to harvest forbids and stamp is a parent willing to write `yes`. The conjunct is graded by the party it constrains, which is precisely what `parent-self-clear` exists to refuse. I am not closing this on "the operator would notice": the deterministic control already in the tree is critic clearance targeting a marker id, and the Proposal replaces it with self-attestation.

*Disposition consequence.* Two coherent leans, and the issue must choose one. (a) Re-open the Stop 1 exclusion: deposit warrant conjuncts as `audit:<id>` markers at write-back, load-bearing, cleared only by a later `role: critic` artifact that names them via `audit-targets:` — and say what happens on open-critique arcs, which have no `refutation-target:` at all. (b) Keep the exclusion and justify a parallel field on grounds other than mechanism, knowing it is self-graded. As drafted the issue does neither and reads as (a) implemented as (b).

---

## Finding 3 — "pain ids" do not exist, and matching without them is the prose parser the issue disclaims

**blocks-the-design**

*Evidence.* Proposal 1: "Stop 1 records `pain:` as a list … One conjunct per item." No id syntax. Proposal 2: "Bound-remedy items cite pain ids they relieve, or `does-not-relieve`." The one instance of this format in the record — recut lean `5655949239` on #4378, posted after this issue was filed — writes a `pain:` field whose value is four unnumbered English bullets: detect-then-confirm; import from other agents; real provenance; blank Phase 1 chat from empty fields. Its coverage table keys on English phrases (`Detect-then-confirm`, `Import from other agents`), not ids, and one row reads `yes via #4377`.

*Failure mode.* A resolver asked to check that Bound-remedy item *k* relieves pain *j* must either match English strings across two hand-written parent artifacts — a prose parser, refused by this issue's own Non-goals and by the contract's `No prose-quality parser (#4309)` — or consume tokens the issue never specifies. The `does-not-relieve` spelling, the `operator-deferred` spelling, and the `yes via #NNNN` partial-relief form are all unpublished. The contract's standard here is hard: *"Publish a form in this list before the parser accepts it. An unpublished spelling is not a citation."*

*Disposition consequence.* Item 2 is not implementable at its current resolution. The lean must publish the id grammar, the closed relief vocabulary, and whether partial relief (`yes via #4377`) counts as relief.

---

## Finding 4 — the missing-field default decides whether the gate exists, and the named fixture cannot run

**blocks-the-design**

*Evidence.* Stop 1 write-back `5654639130` on #4378 carries no `pain:` field. Neither does `5656317654` on this issue. The contract's nearest precedent is explicit fail-open: legacy leans with no target digest stay admitted (#4243).

*Failure mode.* If absent `pain:` admits, the gate is opt-in — and the party that opts in at Stop 1 is the same party that writes the lean and the coverage table, so declining to enumerate pains disables the conjunct with no observer. If absent `pain:` blocks, every arc predating the rule fails closed, and so does every arc whose triage simply forgets the field. The Acceptance sketch names neither branch.

Separately, the fixture named in that sketch is unrunnable: *"#4378 is the fixture: warrant conjuncts vs lean 5654755223 Bound-remedy must fail coverage."* There is no `pain:` list on `5654639130` to fail against. Constructing one now means authoring the pain list with the lean already in hand, which decides the test's outcome before it runs.

*Disposition consequence.* Acceptance criterion 1 and the fixture both need restating. State the missing-field default as a published branch, not an implied one.

---

## Finding 5 — the diagnosis is one layer off, and the cheaper fix is a forcing function

**sharpens-framing**

*Evidence.* The two probe runs above. Clearance is set membership against the **latest** successor lean (`latestSuccessorLean`, `resolveCitedLean`). Posting recut lean `5655949239` withdrew ingest clearance from #4378 deterministically and machine-observably, with no code change and no new field — the verdict flipped from `complete` to `missing-record`. The parent already holds a revocation lever the resolver honours.

*Failure mode addressed.* The gap is therefore not "the resolver never asks about coverage." It is that nothing forces the parent to exercise that lever at the moment it posts the accepted sentence. The Problem section's "the completed-arc record itself must not clear ingest while warrant pain is unrelieved" overstates by one layer: the record has a revocation path and it works; it has no *prompt*.

*Disposition consequence.* This changes what to build. A forcing step at the synthesis-accepted surface — parent posts the coverage reading before the accepted sentence, and an unrelieved row means posting a later successor lean instead of that sentence — survives Finding 1 (it is parent prose and admits it), survives Finding 3 (no id matching; it is a reading, not a parse), and needs no new `CompletedArcBlockReason`. It does not survive Finding 2, which is why Finding 2 is the load-bearing one.

---

## Finding 6 — injection / swarm lens: the pain list is parent-voice work text derived from an untrusted body

**sharpens-framing**

The lens fires: the target changes envelopes and consumes untrusted input.

*Evidence.* `composeOverviewWithComments` (`packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:1326`) copies every comment verbatim and unfenced into the xBRIEF Overview the next worker reads as dispatch input, beneath a line telling it to read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143). The contract already records this hazard for plain-language summaries and answers it by marking both summaries non-normative for downstream agents and forbidding an implementer being addressed in them. Proposal 1 derives `pain:` from the because-clause, which is derived from the issue body — untrusted external content under `## Security context (#480)`.

*Failure mode.* Three, concretely. (i) A body that names no pain yields an empty list and a vacuously-satisfied bind conjunct — the gate is disabled by the untrusted artifact it reads. (ii) Loosely phrased pains let any lean claim relief; the untrusted body sets the bar the parent then grades itself against. (iii) Downstream, `pain:` is an imperative-shaped work list in the parent authoritative voice — "import from other agents", "detect-then-confirm" — sitting unfenced in the ingest-cleared Overview with no non-normative marking. That is the #3929 shape with a new artifact.

*Disposition consequence.* The lean must mark `pain:` and the coverage table non-normative for downstream agents under the existing heading, and must state that the pain list is parent-**authored** from the body rather than lifted from it.

---

## Finding 7 — unclosed token and unnamed reason code, where the contract requires published closed sets

**sharpens-framing**

*Evidence.* Proposal 3: "Token a closed line **such as** `design-critique: pain-unrelieved, because …`". "Such as" is an open set describing a closed one. Meanwhile `COMPLETED_ARC_BLOCK_REASONS` is a nine-member frozen array and the union is derived from it so that a member added without a contract row fails the content-contract suite (#3942); the contract requires a reason be published in that table before the evaluator returns it. Proposal 4 requires the completed-arc record to block, and names no reason code.

I did check the collision surface and it is clean: a `design-critique: pain-unrelieved` line matches neither `SYNTHESIS_SHAPE_RE` nor `CANCELLED_SHAPE_RE`, and a pain-coverage table trips none of the four `### Reserved line-starts` predicates. But that matrix is per-artifact, the new token gets no row, and the new line gets no position predicate — fence, quote, strike, negation.

*Failure mode.* Without a published reason code the Acceptance sketch's "the completed-arc record itself must not clear ingest" cannot be satisfied by any conforming implementation; the implementer either invents an unpublished code (contract violation) or silently downgrades the block to prose. Without a position predicate, a fenced example of the token in a later comment is indistinguishable from an operative one.

*Disposition consequence.* Name the reason code, the exact line spelling, and the position predicate — or scope item 3 to parent prose and drop the completed-arc-record claim.

---

## Finding 8 — recorded spend on the in-envelope Stop 1 write-back is N=1

**footnote**

`5656317654` records `charter: refutation`, spend `N=1`, and "Spend rationale: N=1 … Panel permission is not used." This envelope dispatched N=3 across three seat families. Stop 2 requires the spend recorded as a field. Later comments exist on this thread above my ceiling; I did not read them, so I cannot confirm whether the spend was amended there. I name it only because a post-ceiling amendment to a Stop 2 field is unreadable by every sibling in the round it governs — each sibling's only in-envelope record of this arc's spend says N=1. No disposition consequence for the design.

---

## Finding 9 — anchor drift in the body, and the remedy already ran without code

**footnote**

"Chip is `design-critique:ingest-ready`" was true at filing (20:28:16Z) and stale six minutes later (reverted 20:34:15Z). More usefully: recut lean `5655949239` already carries a `pain:` list and a pain-coverage table, authored with zero code changes, and closes with "This lean does not stamp ingest-ready." The format is reachable as contract text today. That is evidence for Findings 1 and 5 and against the closing "Auto-stamp resolver grows a coverage conjunct." Also, the escalation options listed in the Exemplar section omit the fourth the contract already names: the operator raises the cap for this arc and records it (Dual stop).

---

### Road not taken

I considered filing the whole thing as `sharpens-framing` on the ground that this repo ships unobserved contract obligations on purpose (#3850, #3929, #4309 are all named as unenforced in the contract's own voice), so "the lever is a fixture" would be a category note rather than a block. I rejected it because this issue does not claim to be adding an unobserved obligation — it claims a resolver conjunct and a completed-arc-record block, twice, in the Proposal and the Acceptance sketch. A lean that binds those sentences as written produces a guard that never runs.

### Steelman, and what flips my verdict

The strongest rejected position: a parent-graded coverage table is worth shipping even self-attested, because it converts a silent omission into a visible row, and legibility — not enforcement — is the deliverable. The recut on #4378 is mild support: the table made the four leftovers legible enough to argue about. What would flip Findings 1 and 3 to `sharpens-framing`: a lean that drops "Auto-stamp resolver grows a coverage conjunct" and the completed-arc-record claim, states plainly that the obligation is behavioural and unobserved in the contract's established voice, and scopes the artifact to a parent reading rather than a parse. Finding 2 would survive that revision, because a self-graded conjunct over a self-authored pain list is weaker than the `audit:` marker mechanism already in the tree — and that one is fail-closed, non-self-clearable, and carries its own envelope obligation.
